guide.title: Codex Agent Setup Library
guide.scope: A reference for local Codex, the CLI, the desktop app and cloud agents.

priorities.title: Choose the surface and establish the boundaries
priorities.text: Read the surface map, instruction discovery, config basics, and permissions first. Define the job, allowed sources, write scope, and what counts as done.

priorities.title: Make one agent repeatable
priorities.text: Add a narrow role, reusable skills, a project description, relevant command rules, and a verification routine. Keep the first workflow small enough to inspect.

priorities.title: Add delegation, integrations, and cloud execution
priorities.text: Expand only when the task needs it. Document credentials ownership, tool access, environment preparation, retries, and human review before introducing unattended work.

instruction_notes.title: Instruction discovery
instruction_notes.text: Codex reads personal guidance, then project guidance from the repository root toward the working directory. Within a directory, AGENTS.override.md is selected before AGENTS.md; configured fallback filenames come next. Deeper guidance can refine earlier instructions.

instruction_notes.title: Configuration is a separate layer
instruction_notes.text: Runtime settings use a separate order, highest first: CLI overrides, trusted project layers nearest the working directory, selected profile, user config, cloud-managed defaults, system config, then built-ins. Enforced requirements constrain those defaults.

instruction_notes.title: Roles, skills, and rules have different jobs
instruction_notes.text: A custom agent defines a specialist. A skill describes a repeatable workflow. A command rule evaluates command patterns. Combining them works best when each has one clear responsibility.

instruction_notes.title: Project descriptions need an explicit route
instruction_notes.text: Recommended: link README.md or docs/PROJECT.md from AGENTS.md; ordinary notes are not automatically instruction files.

files.discovery: Selected instead of AGENTS.md in that directory

files.description: Share only project-specific settings; verify current supported keys.
Current profile-file convention; older inline profile tables are retired.
Reusable personal specialist, separate from project ownership.
Reusable task procedure with a clear trigger.
Command matching and decisions; validate before applying.
Keep project command decisions scoped and tested.
Recommended: purpose, domain and success criteria.
Record choices, rationale, dates and unresolved questions.
Authoritative sources, refresh dates and access constraints.
Separate observed evidence from final artifacts; retain verification results.
Use the documented cloud setup flow; local Mac config is not a cloud deployment manifest.

Personal Mac setup (illustrative)
~/.codex/
  AGENTS.md
  config.toml
  <profile>.config.toml          optional selected profile
  agents/<role>.toml
  rules/<policy>.rules
~/.agents/skills/<workflow>/
  SKILL.md
  references/                   optional supporting material
  scripts/                      optional tested helpers

Project setup (illustrative)
project/
  AGENTS.md
  README.md
  .codex/config.toml
  .codex/agents/<role>.toml
  .codex/rules/<policy>.rules
  .agents/skills/<workflow>/SKILL.md
  docs/PROJECT.md                explicitly referenced context
  docs/DECISIONS.md
  docs/SOURCES.md
  <module>/AGENTS.override.md    only when a scoped exception is needed
  reports/
  outputs/

roles.title: Manager / coordinator
roles.description: Own the brief, task boundaries, specialist assignments, shared decisions, and acceptance criteria. Assemble evidence into one deliverable.
roles.minimum: Project brief + AGENTS.md + delegation policy + handoff format
roles.surface: Local coordination first; cloud when continuity is required.

roles.title: Researcher / analyst
roles.description: Collect sources, distinguish observations from inference, record freshness and gaps, and return citations. Add domain-specific data methods as needed.
roles.minimum: Source register + research skill + evidence format + limited tool access
roles.surface: Local for private files; cloud for connected or hosted work.

roles.title: Builder / implementation agent
roles.description: Own a defined set of files, preserve unrelated edits, implement changes, and run relevant tests. Keep deployment authority explicit.
roles.minimum: Project instructions + build/test commands + write scope + review checkpoint
roles.surface: Codex local, CLI, or a reproducible cloud environment.

roles.title: Reviewer / security specialist
roles.description: Inspect a bounded change or artifact and report only evidence-backed issues. Separate review, remediation, and release responsibilities.
roles.minimum: Review criteria + source references + read scope + severity definitions
roles.surface: Local/CLI reviews or configured GitHub cloud reviews.

roles.title: Automation / integration agent
roles.description: Define triggers, inputs, expected outputs, failure handling, checkpoints, and stop conditions. Reconcile uncertain external outcomes before retrying.
roles.minimum: Runbook + tool contract + permissions + retry policy + execution logs
roles.surface: CLI jobs, hosted environments, or an application using the SDK/API.

roles.title: Business operations specialist
roles.description: Add a narrow department playbook for procurement, content, documents, finance, or support. Distinguish drafts from approved external actions.
roles.minimum: Domain brief + source ownership + relevant skills + action boundaries
roles.surface: Local for sensitive documents; Work/dots when supported integrations fit.

brief_fields: What will this agent be hired to produce, for whom, and how will success be checked?
Desktop Codex, CLI, Codex Cloud, Work/dots, or an SDK/API application?
Which files, repositories, sites, and connected tools are authoritative and accessible?
What may it read, edit, send, publish, purchase, or schedule? Who approves exceptions?
Which personal rules apply, which project context is needed, and which workflows should be reusable?
What can be parallelized, who owns each output, and what must return to the manager?
Which checks prove completion, where is evidence saved, and how are partial runs resumed?
What duration, frequency, token/spend limits, and escalation conditions are agreed?

caveats.title: Permission profiles are Beta and version-sensitive
caveats.text: The documented permission profiles do not compose directly with legacy sandbox_mode settings. Choose the intended mechanism after checking the installed version and managed policy.

caveats.title: Instruction size limit wording conflicts
caveats.text: The instruction-size limit is described as combined in AGENTS.md and per-file in Advanced Configuration. Verify loading before relying on either interpretation.

caveats.title: Cloud is more than one product
caveats.text: Codex Cloud, ChatGPT Work/dots, and the Agents API have separate setup and policy surfaces. Account eligibility and tool availability must be checked for the chosen runtime.

caveats.title: Managed Macs have additional precedence rules
caveats.text: The order above is ordinary configuration precedence. Legacy managed defaults and macOS MDM have separate startup precedence; inspect effective configuration on managed Macs.
